title: ALMAGAL: IX. The chemical complexity of AG318.9477−00.1960: A line-identification template for ALMAGAL
question: Characterise the chemical inventory of high-mass core AG318-c9 as a line-identification template for the ALMAGAL survey, and assess whether ethylene glycol, glycolaldehyde, and methyl formate trace the innermost regions of hot molecular cores.

data.arrays: 12 m array and 7 m Atacama Compact Array (7M)
data.sensitivity: continuum rms ~ 0.28 mJy beam^-1; 5 sigma line detection threshold ~ 1.35 K

what.value: Clump and core physical properties for AG318.9477-00.1960 and AG318-c9 (distance, coordinates, continuum fluxes, deconvolved size, mass, density, H2 column density, luminosity, systemic velocity)

evidence.quote: Table notes: Parameters derived from (cite: almagal1) and (cite: almagal3).

The clump has a mass of $M_{\rm clump} \sim 5870\,M_{\odot}$, a luminosity of $L_{\rm clump}\sim 2.7\, \times 10^{5}\,L_{\odot}$, an $L/M$ $\sim 46.5\,\rm L_{\odot}/M_{\odot}$, and a systemic velocity of $V_{\rm lsr}=-34.4$ km s$^{-1}$ (cite: almagal1).

what.value: Spectroscopic catalogues CDMS and JPL accessed via Splatalogue

evidence.quote: For the remaining unidentified lines, we used `Splatalogue` to search for additional molecular species with transitions consistent with the observed frequencies, drawing spectroscopic data from the CDMS (cite: cdms2001; cdms2005; cdms2016) and the JPL (cite: jpl) catalogues.

external_data.citation: CDMS (cite: cdms2001; cdms2005; cdms2016) and JPL (cite: jpl)

what.value: Column densities and abundances of molecular species in hot core G31.41+0.31 from the GUAPOS survey

evidence.loc: Comparison with the hot core G31.41+0.31
evidence.quote: The GUAPOS survey (cite: guapos1; guapos2; guapos3; guapos4; guapos5; GUAPOS6) explored the chemical richness of G31, detecting numerous O- and N-bearing COMs as formamide (HC(O)NH$_2$), methyl isocyanate (CH$_3$NCO), and ethyl isocyanide (C$_2$H$_5$NC).

external_data.citation: (cite: guapos1; guapos2; guapos3; guapos4; guapos5; GUAPOS6)

recipe.goal: Extract core-integrated spectra and select the chemically richest template core
recipe.method: Integrate emission in spw0 and spw1 over the continuum core ellipse defined in the ALMAGAL core catalogue, then sort cores by intensity and S/N of CH3CN K=2 at 220.730 GHz and MF 17(3,14)->16(3,13) at 218.298 GHz, line density (~80 lines GHz^-1), simple kinematics, and core mass.

recipe.goal: Identify molecular lines and fit LTE synthetic spectra to derive physical parameters and abundances
recipe.method: Search for molecular transitions with S/N >= 5 (~1.35 K) using Splatalogue (CDMS and JPL catalogues) and fit LTE synthetic spectra (accounting for line opacity) using SLIM and AUTOFIT in MADCUBA, both manually and via an automated two-round MADCUBA macro. Compute abundances relative to H2 and scale optically thick main isotopologues from rarer isotopologues using Galactocentric isotopic ratios.
key_parameters: Initial guesses: V = -34.4 km s^-1, FWHM = 5 km s^-1, theta_s = 0 (no beam dilution), initial T_ex from rotational diagram of 41 MF transitions (T_ex^CH3OCHO = 167 K)
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), justified by n_H2 = 1.72 x 10^8 cm^-3
N_H2 = 7.35 x 10^24 cm^-2 derived from M_core = 124.2 M_sun, D_core = 6396 au, m_H = 1.67 x 10^-24 g, mu = 2.8

recipe.goal: Compare the chemical inventory and abundances of AG318-c9 with hot core G31.41+0.31
recipe.method: Compare column densities and relative abundances of species covered by both ALMAGAL and the GUAPOS survey of G31.41+0.31 over comparable spatial scales (~6400 au for AG318-c9 vs ~4500 au for G31), and estimate core luminosity by flux-scaling the clump luminosity.
key_parameters: Excluded species not in both setups or with unpublished GUAPOS deuterated data
assumptions: Clump luminosity apportioned to core by ratio of peak continuum flux to sum of all 19 core peak fluxes

recipe.goal: Generate spatially resolved moment 0, N, and T_ex maps and radial profiles for EG, GA, and MF
recipe.method: Generate moment 0, 1, and 2 maps using one representative unblended transition per molecule, then perform pixel-by-pixel LTE fits in MADCUBA SLIM/AUTOFIT on pixels with moment 0 S/N > 3, and average values within concentric 0.1'' annuli to derive radial profiles.
key_parameters: Moment map transitions: GA 35(10,26)->35(9,27) at 220.055 GHz, EG 24(1,24)->23(1,23) at 217.45 GHz, MF 17(3,14)->16(3,13) at 218.298 GHz; pixel threshold S/N > 3; annulus width 0.1''
assumptions: Single-species LTE fit per pixel without contribution from other blending molecules

answer_key.quantity: Total detected molecular species in AG318-c9

evidence.quote: We report the detection of 65 molecular species, including 31 main species and 34 isotopologues and vibrationally excited species.

Overall, the identified molecular inventory reveals a chemically rich environment dominated by oxygen-bearing species (44), followed by nitrogen-bearing (28), sulphur-bearing (8), and silicon-bearing (2), with COMs accounting for more than half of the detections (33).
A total of 91 lines remained unassigned and are labelled unidentified (U) in the spectra.
The resulting fit of the detected transitions of GA indicates $T_{\rm ex} = 168\pm 13\,$K, $N=(1.45\pm 0.12)\times 10^{16}\,\rm cm^{-2}$ and $V=-36.89 \pm 0.1\,\rm km\,s^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Estimated core luminosity L_core of AG318-c9

evidence.loc: Comparison with the hot core G31.41+0.31
evidence.quote: We apportioned the clump luminosity to AG318$-$c9 by scaling it by the ratio of its peak flux ($F_{\rm peak_{core}}$) to the sum of all the core peak fluxes ($F_{\rm peak_{all\ cores}}$), leading to $L_{\rm core}\approx 1.2 \times 10^5\,L_{\odot}$, which is almost three times higher than the luminosity of G31.

evidence.quote: The $T_{\rm ex}(\rm MF)$ map (Fig. [10](#fig:maps)) shows a robust temperature gradient, rising from $\sim 100\,$K in the outer parts of the core up to $\sim 250\,$K towards the centre.

evidence.loc: Integrated intensity, $T_{\rm ex}$, and $N$ maps of EG, GA, and MF
evidence.quote: Because MF has the most unblended transitions, its $T_{\rm ex}$ map has the lowest relative error ($\frac{\Delta T_{\rm ex}}{T_{\rm ex}} \sim 10\,\%$), which increases only in the outer regions with a lower S/N (Appendix [9.1](#error_maps)).

score_reason: The spectral analysis recipe is thoroughly documented (including flowcharts, initial seeds, transition tables, and public MADCUBA scripts on GitHub) and all derived parameters are tabulated; minor deductions only because cube imaging/calibration is deferred to ALMAGAL Paper II and exact velocity integration windows for moment maps are unstated.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA project 2019.1.00195.L data are public, the analysis scripts and transition lists are publicly released on GitHub, and the paper provides a complete quantitative table of T_ex, N, FWHM, V, and X for 65 species as an answer key.
